Subject: Requirements: Private deployment across EU & APAC — residency and failover

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the quick intro call. We’re evaluating Redwood for a private deployment (VPC) that must span our EU and APAC regions. A few non-negotiables from legal/security/procurement:

- Data residency: customer PII and health metadata must remain in-region (EU data must not leave EU jurisdiction).
- Failover: we need a documented cross-region continuity plan — RTO < 15min for control plane metadata, RPO for token logs acceptable up to 1 hour if encrypted.
- Network: private peering with our cloud regions (Azure EU, GCP APAC), strict inbound rules, and service endpoints behind NGFWs.
- Key management: integration with our KMS/HSM and ability for us to manage keys; bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) required.

Can you confirm whether Redwood’s Private control plane can be configured to keep CRUD operations and logs in-region, and outline how you handle KV cache replication and failover between regions? Any example topology or checklist would be helpful.

Best,
Sara Kim
Director of Cloud Ops
Orchid Health

Sara — thanks for the clear list. High level: yes, we support region-scoped Private control planes and can keep control-plane metadata and token logs in-region with customer-managed KMS. That said, the exact topology and SLAs depend on whether you want active-active across regions or an active-primary + warm standby.

Quick clarifying Qs so we can give a precise ops design:
1) Do you require active-active inference (serving) for production traffic in both EU and APAC, or would APAC be a standby for EU (or vice-versa)?
2) For telemetry and traces, are you OK with aggregated metrics being routed through a central observability aggregator outside region, or must all monitoring data be region-bound?
3) Who on your infra side manages peering & firewall rules (we’ll need an admin contact and a jumpbox host for initial testing)?

I’m looping in Karthik (inference infra) and Laura (eng sales ops) to draft an ops-ready plan and a residency checklist. We’ll attach a proposed network diagram and a short failover playbook.

Thanks — Vivek

Sara — attaching a first-pass architecture and checklist. TL;DR: we recommend an active-primary (EU) + warm-standby (APAC) for stateful control-plane items with cross-region replication of model artifacts and shards. Serving nodes can be regional to preserve latency; a global routing layer (customer-managed DNS + health checks) can fail traffic to APAC on region outage.

Key points (short):
- Control plane: deploy control-plane services inside each region VPC. Use per-region Postgres (or managed equivalent) for control metadata; encrypted at rest with your KMS keys. Replication between DBs is configured as async (to respect residency rules) with manual promotion during failover.
- Logs & token material: store logs in-region. For compliance we ship an option to keep token telemetry in-region and export aggregated anonymized metrics to a central observability instance only if you opt in.
- KV cache & model shards: model weights/artifacts are replicated via our artifact sync service; cache (KV) is regional-only by default. For active-active serving, KV sync would add cross-region traffic and complexity.
- Network topology: private VPC peering (or AWS Transit/GCP Interconnect equivalents), explicit egress whitelists, and a TLS-terminating edge inside the customer VPC.
- KMS: BYOK supported, with customer HSM/KMS in each region. Keys never leave customer control.

I’ve included two attachments: network-diagram-eu-apac.svg and residency-checklist-v2.pdf (checklist maps to your legal asks, RTO/RPO options, and network changes). Also drafting a short failover playbook we can operationalize with your SREs.

Attachment stubs:

- residency-checklist-v2.pdf (PDF, 8 pages)

Sara — looping in procurement/contracting ownership. We can provide a DPA addendum and a BYOK clause; attaching a draft data-processing-addendum.docx for your legal team to review. A couple of notes:

- The DPA will state that control-plane metadata and token logs are stored in the designated regions and that key material under BYOK remains under your control.
- For the failover playbook: we typically run a joint tabletop with the customer SREs and our Platform Ops team. That runbook includes steps for DB promotion, DNS failover, and cache warm-up. In most runbooks the RTO for control-plane promotion (manual + automated checks) is 10–20 minutes depending on DNS TTLs; we include a presigned automation package to reduce manual latency.
- Regarding SSH/bastion: we do not require persistent inbound SSH to your private subnets. Initial deployment can be done via a temporary, auditable bastion or via customer-side deployment scripts (preferred).

Attachment stub: data-processing-addendum.docx (Word, 6 pages)

If it helps, we can propose a phased acceptance plan:
1) Install control plane in EU only (smoke tests + residency verification)
2) Standby APAC deployment with artifact sync (no traffic) — failover tabletop
3) Optional active-active serving cutover (if you want lower latency in APAC)

Happy to schedule a walkthrough with Markus and your SREs next week.
